title: Sex-Dependent Impact of Low-Level Lead Exposure during Prenatal Period on Child Psychomotor Functions.
ehr_evidence: The study utilized the Polish Mother and Child Cohort (REPRO_PL), collecting questionnaire data, biological samples, and neurodevelopmental assessments directly from participants.
summary: Prospective mother-child cohort study evaluating the sex-dependent impact of low-level prenatal lead exposure on child psychomotor and cognitive development up to 24 months of age.
key_findings: Among boys, increasing cord blood lead levels were associated with lower cognitive function scores (β = −2.07; p = 0.04).
No statistically significant impact of prenatal lead exposure on girls' psychomotor abilities was observed.
For language and motor abilities, results were not statistically significant for either sex (p > 0.05).
captured_features: blood lead levels (2nd trimester and cord blood)
Bayley cognitive, language, and motor scores
population: 402 children from the Polish Mother and Child Cohort (REPRO_PL) in Poland, assessed up to 24 months of age
limitations: no measurement of lead levels in children's blood
lack of data on home environment quality, parent-child relationship, parental roles, and maternal IQ
potential selection bias as sample represents urban population with high SES
lack of measurement/inclusion of other neurotoxic elements (As, Cd, Hg)
